title: Role shadow and handoff runbook — 30-day accelerator
summary: Lightweight, repeatable runbook to accelerate role transitions: targeted at managers and People Ops running a 30-day shadow + handoff for internal transfers, contractor conversions, and new hire accelerators. Contains day-by-day checklist, a short interview-calibration rubric for final-stage hires, and sign-off template.
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic runbook to ensure role knowledge transfer and ramp in the first 30 days when someone is leaving a role (internal transfer, contractor finish, or permanent role transition) and a new person is stepping in. The aim is to reduce tribal knowledge loss, set clear success signals, and create repeatable artifacts that scale across teams.

Audience:
- Hiring manager or receiving manager
- People Ops partner supporting the transition
- Outgoing role owner (shadow giver)
- Incoming person (shadow receiver) or candidate about to start
- Solutions / infra owners for any cross-team dependencies

High-level flow:
1) Plan phase (before last week of outgoing owner)
2) Shadow phase (first 10–14 days overlap; live paired work)
3) Handoff artifacts & dry run (days 10–20)
4) Autonomy & watchful support (days 20–30)
5) Sign-off + retro (end of day 30)

Before you start (checklist for manager / People Ops):
- Confirm overlap window and calendar blocks for 2–4 hours/day of paired time (Outgoing + Incoming).
- Book a 60-minute kickoff meeting: expectations, communication norms, escalation path.
- Identify 5 critical scenarios the new person must be comfortable with by day 30. (List below.)
- Reserve time for team demos, code walkthroughs, and runbooks.
- Add both people to ops/infra alerts and dashboards with read-only where appropriate.
- Create a shared folder: role-handbook + lightweight runbook + must-know links.
- Create a GitHub/GitLab board or Jira sprint with the top 10 transfer tickets (labeled handoff).
- Notify downstream teams (product, SRE, support) and schedule alignment syncs.

Critical scenarios (examples — customize per role):
- Recovering a failed production job and rolling back a model endpoint.
- Adding a new model variant and validating perf/latency.
- Running the weekly cost/usage report and interpreting anomalies.
- Shipping a Hotfix: PR -> review -> deploy -> monitoring -> rollback.
- On-call escalation: pager workflow and runbook triggers.

Shadow phase (days 1–14):
- Day 1: Kickoff, shared folder walkthrough, 30-minute "where things live" tour. Set three micro-goals for week 1.
- Days 2–3: Paired observation — incoming watches outgoing handle live incidents or routine tasks. Notes: capture command snippets, dashboards, and scripts.
- Day 4: Reverse shadow — incoming explains a previously observed flow while outgoing coaches.
- Days 5–7: Focused deep dives: one day each for infra, deployment, and customer-facing processes.
- Days 8–10: Live pairing on real tasks with outgoing as second pair. Aim for 70/30 split (incoming does 70%).
- Days 11–14: Run three dry runs of a critical scenario end-to-end with minimal prompts. Document deviations.

Handoff artifacts (must be completed by day 14):
- Role handbook (single page summary) with: primary responsibilities, key stakeholders, daily/weekly/monthly tasks, and escalation points.
- Top 10 runbook commands/scripts with short descriptions.
- Architecture diagram (high level) + link to full diagrams.
- List of active tickets or initiatives with owner/next action.
- Access list: systems, dashboards, repos, and who to contact if access fails.
- On-call schedule and playbook excerpt.

Dry run sessions (template):
- Goal: accomplish scenario X end-to-end without prompts.
- Start with 10-minute context recap.
- 45–60-minute execution window.
- 15-minute debrief: what went well, gaps, follow-up actions.
- Document into shared folder and tag JIRA handoff ticket.

30-day success signals (examples to use as KPI for ramp):
- Incoming can resolve the defined critical scenario without help in under target time (e.g., restore infra in <30 min).
- Can explain architecture and deployment flow to a peer in 15 minutes.
- Completed 3 owner-verified tickets from the handoff board.
- No unresolved access or permissions issues after day 7.
- Positive team feedback in the 30-day retro.

Sign-off & retro (end of day 30):
- Manager, outgoing, and incoming meet for 45 minutes. Review artifacts, open action items, and document the final handbook.
- Fill short sign-off template: "I, [name], confirm that I am comfortable owning [scope] with the listed exceptions: [exceptions]."
- Capture 3 improvements to the runbook for next time. Add to Confluence page (CON-12345).

Quick interview calibration rubric (for last-stage hires or internal candidates — short form):
- Use for final-stage practical interview or job trial assessment when you need to compare candidates fairly during handoff hires.
- Scoring: 1–4 scale (1: insufficient, 2: developing, 3: meets bar, 4: exceeds bar).
- Dimensions (pick top 4 relevant):
  - System knowledge (breadth of architecture + core components)
  - Troubleshooting under pressure (practical repair scenario)
  - Ownership & communication (stakeholder updates, ticket hygiene)
  - Tooling fluency (CI/CD, monitoring, infra-as-code)
- Example rubric row (to paste into scorecard):
  - System knowledge: 1: can't articulate key components. 2: knows components but misses dependencies. 3: explains architecture and tradeoffs. 4: identifies failure modes and mitigations.
  - Troubleshooting: 1: panics or stalls. 2: finds direction with strong hints. 3: isolates root cause and proposes fix. 4: executes fix and writes mitigation plan.

Calibration notes:
- Use the same scenario for all candidates and give 40–60 minutes.
- Collect scores and a 1–2 sentence rationale per dimension.
- If score spread >1.0 for any dimension, schedule a short calibration call among interviewers to reconcile.

Lightweight 30/60/90 template (to adapt per role):
- 30: understand systems, complete 3 handoff tickets, shadow support rotations.
- 60: own routine ops, lead one cross-team sync, start contributing to medium initiative.
- 90: independently own on-call rotation, drive a small project end-to-end, present learnings to team.

Notes to self (working doc style):
- Keep this doc concise — teams want checklists not essays.
- Link back to CON-12345 and update with concrete examples from infra, hosting, or product teams.
- For contractors converting to full time: ensure compensation/hiring coordinator sync happens by day 10.
- Edge cases: very small overlap (0–1 day) — escalate to manager to schedule asynchronous video recordings + 2 weeks of paired office hours.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Add a short template for "must-know commands" that is language-agnostic.
- Validate the rubric with hiring managers in infra and serving-runtime.
- Create a quick Loom template for dry run recordings.

References and links:
- CON-12345: master runbooks index (Confluence)
- JIRA-9876: handoff sprint board
- Slack: #people-ops, #eng-oncall
- Example sign-off: "handoff-signoff-template.docx" (upload to shared folder)

Quick timeline estimate for manager (time investment):
- Planning and kickoff: 2–3 hours
- Shadowing commitments: 2–3 hours/day first 10 days (may be split into smaller blocks)
- Dry runs and docs: 4–6 hours total across weeks 2–3
- Retro/sign-off: 1 hour

If you use this runbook: please add your team name and 1 example improvement next to the retro note so we can iterate.

-- End of runbook (draft) --
notes: Informal doc style: mix of checklists, templates, and TODOs. Meant to be copied and adapted per team. Keep it short and practical.
